title: Atypical HUS: Alternative Complement Gene Variants and Terminal C5 Inhibition
subject: ss-paediatric-nephrology

steps.say: Atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome is driven by uncontrolled complement activation destroying vascular endothelium.
steps.tx: Map genetic pathogenic drivers within the **Atypical HUS genetic landscape** to identify primary thrombotic microangiopathy mechanisms. Atypical HUS represents uncontrolled alternative complement activation on host endothelial surfaces, driven predominantly by loss-of-function mutations in regulatory protective proteins including CFH, CFI, and CD46/MCP, or by gain-of-function mutations in active convertase components C3 and CFB.

vis.title: Alternative Complement Pathway Genetic Alterations
rows: Failed protection of self endothelial cell surfaces

steps.say: Factor H mutations represent the most frequent genetic aberration and carry poor natural prognosis.
steps.tx: Assess prognosis by determining the **Complement Factor H (CFH) variant frequency** in presenting pediatric cohorts. Heterozygous or homozygous mutations in CFH located on chromosome 1q31.3 account for 25-30% of all atypical HUS cases, historically carrying a devastating 70% risk of progressing to end-stage renal disease or death within 1 year of onset without anti-complement therapy.

left.title: CFH Genetic Variants
points: 70% ESRD or mortality within 1 year if untreated

right.title: Therapeutic Transformation
points: Responsive to prompt terminal complement inhibition

steps.say: Acquired autoantibodies against factor H represent a distinct treatable immunological subgroup.
steps.tx: Screen for circulating autoantibodies identifying **Anti-factor H autoantibody HUS and CFHR1-3 deletion** patterns in childhood. Circulating anti-CFH autoantibodies cause 10-15% of pediatric atypical HUS (forming the predominant etiology in India), strongly linked to homozygous deletion of CFHR1-CFHR3 genes; management mandates therapeutic plasma exchange paired with pulsed oral prednisolone and rituximab to suppress autoantibody synthesis.

steps.say: Terminal complement blockade blocks cell destruction and restores native microvascular patency.
steps.tx: Arrest microvascular thrombosis using the protocolized **Eculizumab terminal C5 blockade protocol** immediately upon diagnosis. Eculizumab, a recombinant humanized anti-C5 monoclonal antibody, binds cleavage fragment C5 to prevent terminal membrane attack complex (C5b-9) assembly and leukocyte chemotaxis, reliably inducing complete hematologic remission and substantial renal recovery in > 80% of treated atypical HUS patients.

vis.title: Eculizumab Monoclonal Antibody Profile
rows: Prevents generation of C5a and C5b
Permits recovery of native renal filtration

steps.say: Inhibiting terminal complement creates immense vulnerability to encapsulated meningococcal organisms.
steps.tx: Instituting terminal blockade necessitates strict adherence to **Meningococcal prophylaxis requirement** standards before drug delivery. Terminal complement blockade increases individual patient susceptibility to invasive Neisseria meningitidis by 2000-fold; mandatory immunization with conjugated MenACWY and recombinant MenB vaccines combined with daily oral prophylactic penicillin or erythromycin must be initiated immediately alongside eculizumab.

vis.title: Mandatory Meningococcal Protection Protocol
rows: Capsular protective antibodies against serogroups A,C,W,Y
Protects against prevalent serogroup B strains

steps.say: Engineered long-acting inhibitors offer extended maintenance intervals that dramatically reduce hospital burden.
steps.tx: Optimize outpatient maintenance convenience by selecting the **Ravulizumab extended-interval C5 inhibitor** formulation for ongoing suppression. Ravulizumab is an engineered long-acting C5 monoclonal inhibitor with histidine-swapped Fc recycling providing an extended terminal elimination half-life, requiring intravenous maintenance infusions only once every 8 weeks in children weighing >= 20 kg, or every 4 weeks if < 20 kg.

left.title: Eculizumab Regimen
points: Higher frequency of vascular access strain

steps.say: Surface-bound regulator defects allow successful renal allografting without fears of disease recurrence.
steps.tx: Evaluate post-transplant risk stratifying by **CD46 / MCP mutation transplant outcomes** during pre-transplant assessment. Isolated membrane cofactor protein (CD46/MCP) mutations carry a low risk of post-transplant recurrence (< 20%), because unlike soluble circulating factors, CD46 is a transmembrane protein expressed natively by donor graft endothelium, providing normal intrinsic local complement regulation within the newly transplanted allograft.

left.title: CD46 / MCP Mutations
points: Low recurrence risk in renal allografts (< 20%)
Donor allograft carries normal protective CD46

right.title: CFH / CFI Mutations
points: Circulating plasma regulators produced in liver
Requires prophylactic C5 inhibitor or combined liver-kidney transplant

steps.say: Unusual non-complement pathways present in early infancy and prove completely refractory to biologic inhibitors.
steps.tx: Identify atypical non-complement phenotypes by investigating **DGKE non-complement atypical HUS** in neonates. Biallelic mutations in diacylglycerol kinase epsilon (DGKE) cause an infantile recessively inherited thrombotic microangiopathy without complement activation, manifesting before age 1 with relapsing nephrotic-range proteinuria and microvascular thrombosis that proves uniformly refractory to eculizumab or ravulizumab terminal complement inhibitors.

vis.title: DGKE Recessive Microangiopathy Features
rows: Requires aggressive supportive care and ACEi
